queries.hook: I'm anxious about how things will turn out. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
hook.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
hook.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
hook.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
hook.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
hook.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

alternates.speaker: Yudhishthira
alternates.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
alternates.sanskrit: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा / मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात्
alternates.line: The mind is faster than the wind, and worries outnumber the blades of grass.
alternates.translation: Yaksha: 'What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than blades of grass?' Yudhishthira: 'A mother is heavier than the earth; a father is higher than the sky; the mind is faster than the wind; worries are more numerous than blades of grass.'
alternates.why: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

prasang.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.story_hook: Four brothers lay dead by a clear lake, and the voice that killed them was asking Yudhishthira riddles.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

alternates.speaker: Tulsidas
alternates.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
alternates.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
alternates.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
alternates.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.

verse.speaker: Janaka
verse.setting: Janaka, having chosen to keep ruling, talks gently to his own restless mind at night.
verse.sanskrit: यथा यथा विकल्पौघान्संकल्पयसि हेलया । तथा तथैति स्फारत्वं संसारस्तव चिन्तया ॥
verse.line: The more scenarios you spin, the bigger your world of worry grows.
verse.translation: The more you casually spin up fancies and possibilities, the more your world of troubles swells, through your own worrying.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.for_you: Your mind is spinning out next month's promotion before it arrives, and that spinning is making the waiting room feel huge. The possibilities you rehearse are building a world of trouble that does not exist yet. Let the calendar rest, and let the conversation come when it comes.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought you are spinning. Let it go without rehearsing it once more.
verse.scene_line: You sit beside Janaka as he gently tells his own mind that the spinning is the source of the swelling.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
the swelling is traced to the spinning, which can be stopped

verse.setting: Poem 'Hold On Yet a While, Brave Heart', second stanza.
verse.line: No winter was but summer came behind,
verse.translation: No winter was but summer came behind, Each hollow crests the wave, They push each other in light and shade; Be steady then and brave.
verse.why: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

prasang.title: 'Hold on yet a while, brave heart' (poem to the Maharaja of Khetri)
prasang.summary: A short poem of encouragement to a friend. Clouds hide the sun for a while, summer always follows winter, and no honest struggle is wasted even when hopes fail.
prasang.lesson: No struggle is wasted; hold on a little longer.

verse.for_you: You check the calendar and rehearse the conversation, waiting for the result that will not arrive until next month. The mind will not settle because the season of waiting is still winter. Be steady, and know that summer comes behind.
verse.try_today: Notice the next thought about the promotion, and let it pass without rehearsing the conversation.
verse.scene_line: The hollow crests the wave and pushes the next in light and shade, so you can be steady and brave.

verse.speaker: Bhushunda
verse.setting: Bhushunda, the ancient crow, tells Vasishtha why he lives long and well.
verse.sanskrit: किमद्य मम संपन्नं प्रातर्वा भविता पुनः । इति चिन्ताज्वरो नास्ति तेन जीवाम्यनामयः ॥
verse.line: 'What happened today? What comes tomorrow?' I don't run that fever. That's why I live well.
verse.translation: 'What has happened to me today? What will come tomorrow?' I have no such fever of worry; so I live long, free of illness.
verse.why: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

prasang.title: Bhushunda, the crow who outlived the ages
prasang.summary: Vasishtha travels to a wish-fulfilling tree on Mount Meru to meet Bhushunda, a crow who has watched world-ages come and go. Asked how he has lived so long, untroubled, Bhushunda lists his habits: he doesn't brood on the past or future, doesn't fret about what he'll get next, doesn't grow arrogant from knowing, and shares in others' joys and sorrows.
prasang.story_hook: High on a mountain lived a crow who had watched whole ages of the world rise and fall.
prasang.lesson: A long, steady life comes from a mind that stays in the present, wants little and stays kind.

verse.for_you: You are caught in the fever of what is next and what has passed. The mind rehearses a conversation it cannot yet have. Let the unknown month remain unknown, and let your rest be your own.
verse.try_today: Notice the calendar check, and let the mind rest on the present moment instead.
verse.scene_line: Bhushunda watches the ages turn without fever, and you watch the calendar with it.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
worry is called a fever he does not run

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.for_you: The results will come when they come, and your manager's calendar will not tell you before then. You can meet the work in front of you without rehearsing a single conversation. The world does not sink those who do the work at hand.

verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: नैव राज्ञा दरः कार्यो जातु कस्यांचिदापदि / अथ चेदपि दीर्णः स्यान्नैव वर्तेत दीर्णवत्
verse.line: In a crisis, you may be shaken inside. Don't let fear make your decisions for you.
verse.translation: A leader should never show fear in any crisis. Even if shaken inside, he should not act like a shaken man.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.misuse: This is about not acting from panic, not about hiding your feelings from everyone.
